label: churn100-s5
summary: This churn model (training AUC 0.901) adds five parts on the logit scale. The strongest is a customer-service-call gate: after a few calls the predicted risk climbs steeply for customers with low or average daytime use, while heavy daytime users are barely affected by calls (training customers with many calls and a below-average day charge churned at 75.6%, n = 156; switching the part off lowers the AUC to 0.759). Heavy daytime use is a second route: risk rises with daytime minutes and steepens once a hinge opens for the heaviest users (1002 customers past the hinge churned at 28.4%, against 9.4% for the rest). An international plan is the third route (380 holders churned at 42.4%), and a voice-mail plan lowers the risk. Per-state offsets (up for California and Washington, down for Vermont) follow the direction of the state churn rates but are larger than the state counts warrant, and a mild account-length rise adds little (the AUC moves from 0.901 to 0.899 without it). Coverage is complete and the parts reproduce the network to within 4.4e-16.
